title: Two documents in the July 1977 Scientology search inventories, LA 47-12230 (FOIPA 1731044-000)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request concerns two items listed in the FBI inventories of documents seized in the July 1977 searches of Church of Scientology offices in Los Angeles. Both inventories were released to me under FOIPA Request No. 1731044-000 (FBI letter of June 26, 2026). I already hold that release, so please do not send it again. The two released pages are attached.

The items:

(A) Los Angeles file 47-12230, document log page 2, item 11 (container described as a pending basket on a desk): "Letter from [redacted] to [redacted] dated 28 June, 1977, re: El Paso, Texas Msn: [redacted]". This is page 124 of release file D165864264.

(B) Los Angeles file 47-12230, item 9: "Two page letter dated August 6, 1977, re [redacted] in El Paso." This is page 474 of release file D165864264.

I request:

1. Copies of the two documents described in items (A) and (B), if the FBI retained copies, photographs or abstracts of them. Please search file 47-12230, including its exhibit (1A) and bulky exhibit (1B) sections and any sub-files, and the headquarters and Washington Field Office files on the July 1977 searches.

2. A new review of the withholdings in the subject lines of items (A) and (B). These documents were seized more than 49 years ago, and individuals named in them may now be deceased. Please release any part of each subject line that does not identify a private individual. The public interest is in the FBI's own record of the Guardian's Office operations it was investigating, which included operations directed at federal agencies. For item (B), please identify the statute relied on under exemption (b)(3).

3. If the FBI did not retain copies, any record showing what became of the originals: transfer to the National Archives, retention as exhibits in United States v. Mary Sue Hubbard et al., Crim. No. 78-401 (D.D.C.), or return under court order.

Please process each numbered part separately if that is faster. Please release all reasonably segregable material and mark each exemption at the point where material is withheld.

I am an independent historical researcher and ask to be placed in the "all other requesters" fee category. Please contact me before fees exceed $25. If any part of this request is unclear, please contact me so that I can narrow it rather than have it closed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure
